newsitem.title: FRANCE: Thomson-CSF private sale likely - government source.
newsitem.headline: Thomson-CSF private sale likely - government source.

text.p: The French government is likely to privatise defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF through a private placement rather than a public offer, a government source said on Tuesday.
"The chances for a private placement are strong," the source said. "A private placement would allow a faster (defence sector) restructuring."
The source also said the government would announce the sale terms before the end of the week or "at the latest at the beginning of next week".

Government officials at the defence, finance and industry ministries and at the prime minister's office refused to comment, as did Finance Minister Jean Arthuis, when asked about similar reports in French newspapers.
"The government will have the occasion to state its position on this matter in the coming days," Arthuis said.
The government has pledged to announce its plans for the sale of Thomson-CSF before the end of the month.
Financial dailies Les Echos and La Tribune said on Tuesday the sale would be through a private placement, following up a similar report in afternoon daily Le Monde on Monday.
Thomson-CSF is 58-percent held by Thomson SA , which is wholly owned by the state.
Alcatel Alsthom and Lagardere Groupe bid to acquire Thomson-CSF in the original privatisation attempt last October.
The government stated its preference at the time for an offer from Lagardere for all of Thomson SA, which also owns consumer electronics firm Thomson Multimedia (TMM), over a rival bid from Alcatel.

Lagardere planned an onward sale of TMM to South Korea's Daewoo Electronics but the government cancelled the procedure in December after the independent Privatisation Commission said it could not approve the terms of the deal.
The commission objected particularly to the involvement of Daewoo, which had been harshly criticised by French opposition politicians and TMM employees.
The sale's cancellation caused a diplomatic spat with Korea and drew scorn from French and international media commentators, who accused the French government of incompetence in the matter.
Forced to rethink, the government announced afterwards that it would sell its Thomson-CSF stake and TMM separately.
Alcatel has since boosted its position for the acquisition by lining up state-owned aircraft and defence firm Aerospatiale and Dassault Aviation for a joint bid.
